title: Global inverse-image sections respect a commutative square
statement: Let S,T,D,U,E be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms f:T\to S, k:D\to T, d:E\to D, p:U\to T and v:E\to U. Let g:D\to S, r:U\to S and t:E\to S satisfy k;f=g, p;f=r, d;g=t, v;r=t and d;k=v;p, where semicolon denotes composition in traversal order. Let F be a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] on the small etale site of S [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let a be a global section of f^{-1}F. For composable maps f,k and an equality k;f=g, define P_{f,k}^g(a) by the adjunction unit along k, restriction to the identity etale object using its canonical pullback lift [def-pc-fibre-product], the chosen unit-compatible composition comparison c_{f,k} [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and transport along k;f=g. Then P_{g,d}^t(P_{f,k}^g(a))=P_{r,v}^t(P_{f,p}^r(a)). The square need only commute; it need not be cartesian. No connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A3H, final paragraph, identification of the two restrictions through the geometric fibre; formal composition argument from Sites Tags 03CB and 03CC

proof.text: Global unit-restriction is natural in the sheaf: apply the sheaf-naturality clause of the inverse-image units, then naturality of the pulled-back sheaf morphism along the terminal-object lift.

Prove that restricting successively along f and k, then applying c_{f,k}, equals direct restriction along k;f. Apply the composition unit equation at the identity object, restrict it along the composite terminal lift, and use object-naturality of the unit. The two terminal lifts into the pullback of the identity etale object coincide because that target is terminal: base change preserves finite limits, and the identity object is terminal. This is Mathlib Over.mkIdTerminal and IsTerminal.isTerminalObj.

Apply associativity of the composition comparisons at the identity object of E, on the twice restricted section a. Sheaf-naturality of restriction and the preceding unit-restriction composition formula turn each iterated P into direct P along the composite map to T, followed by the associativity equality transport.

Eliminate the equalities defining g,r,t. The two remaining composites E to T are d;k and v;p. Their equality identifies the direct restriction and comparison expressions by equality induction. Composition of Eq.mp transports and proof irrelevance identify the remaining equality proofs. Thus the two iterated P expressions are equal.

theorem etaleSet_globalSection_square
    {S T D U E : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) (k : D ⟶ T) (d : E ⟶ D)
    (p : U ⟶ T) (v : E ⟶ U) (g : D ⟶ S) (r : U ⟶ S) (t : E ⟶ S)
    (hk : k ≫ f = g) (hp : p ≫ f = r)
    (hd : d ≫ g = t) (hv : v ≫ r = t) (hsq : d ≫ k = v ≫ p)
    (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (a : ((L f).obj F).obj.obj (op I[T])) :
    P[g,d,t,hd,F] (P[f,k,g,hk,F] a) =
      P[r,v,t,hv,F] (P[f,p,r,hp,F] a)
